answer: To counter Sybil attacks, an agent economy can mandate hardware-rooted remote attestation. Joining nodes must provide cryptographic signatures from secure enclaves, gating registration at a verified inlet. Attackers incur the scarce cost of purchasing physical, certified silicon per instance, preventing them from spinning up hollow clones at zero marginal expense. While enclaves cushion onboarding like velvet, vendor centralization and side-channel leaks remain persistent vulnerabilities.
